sections.heading: C — Getting Started
sections.markdown:
## C — Getting Started

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A44
Consult the vehicle owner’s manual for its starting procedure. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A44
In the park-and-drive starting sequence described, begin with the selector in park and apply the brake. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A44
Switch the ignition on to check warning lights and gauges before engaging the engine. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A44
After starting in the described sequence, switch on low-beam headlights and lock the doors. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A44
Before moving forward in drive, check ahead, to the sides and behind, signal, then accelerate gradually. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A44
Operate the accelerator with the front of the foot while keeping the heel on the floor. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A44
The clutch friction point is where the engine and transmission begin engaging as the pedal is released. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A44
As you release a manual clutch, match the vehicle’s forward or reverse movement with accelerator pressure. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A44
To start moving a manual vehicle, hold the brake with the right foot and press the clutch fully down with the left. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A44
Select first gear and release the parking brake before moving off in the manual-start sequence. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A44
Signal the intended direction, check mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic before moving off. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A44
Ease the clutch to the friction point while looking toward the road rather than at your hands or feet. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A44
Move the right foot from brake to accelerator, add gentle acceleration and finish releasing the clutch slowly. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A44
A forward jerk during a manual start can mean the clutch was released abruptly or too much accelerator was applied. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A44
If the vehicle lurches and stalls during the described manual start, insufficient accelerator input is the stated cause. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A44
Choose gears according to the driving task’s required power and speed; first gear supplies starting power. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A44
The manual gives 15 to 25 miles per hour as a second-gear example, depending on engine power and whether the transmission has 3, 4 or 5 speeds. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A44
Second gear can also be used to start on ice or drive through heavy snow. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A44
For a 3-speed transmission, the manual generally describes third gear for speeds above 25 miles per hour. [A44] [A45]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A45
For a small-engine vehicle with a 4- or 5-speed transmission, the third-gear example extends to 30 or 40 miles per hour. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A45
The manual describes fourth gear for driving above 35 miles per hour on a flat road. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A45
Uphill driving may require reaching 40 miles per hour or more before selecting fourth or fifth gear. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A45
Before an upshift, accelerate to a speed suitable for the intended gear, press the clutch fully down and release the accelerator. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A45
Complete an upshift by selecting the next higher gear, applying accelerator input and progressively releasing the clutch. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A45
Downshifting can provide more power, assist acceleration or steering, and help slow or stop the vehicle. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A45
Downshifting to slow a descent is advised except when the road is slippery. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A45
For a downshift, release the accelerator and use the brake as well if you want to slow. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

Misconceptions: the steering-direction rule also applies in reverse. [A46]
Mnemonic: check, signal, move smoothly, stop smoothly.
Glossary: the friction point is where clutch release begins connecting engine and transmission. [A44]
Dynamic facts: model-specific gear ranges and local idling ordinances need their stated conditions.

ranked.label: Consult the vehicle owner’s manual for its starting procedure.
In the park-and-drive starting sequence described, begin with the selector in park and apply the brake.
Switch the ignition on to check warning lights and gauges before engaging the engine.
After starting in the described sequence, switch on low-beam headlights and lock the doors.
Before moving forward in drive, check ahead, to the sides and behind, signal, then accelerate gradually.
Operate the accelerator with the front of the foot while keeping the heel on the floor.
The clutch friction point is where the engine and transmission begin engaging as the pedal is released.
As you release a manual clutch, match the vehicle’s forward or reverse movement with accelerator pressure.
To start moving a manual vehicle, hold the brake with the right foot and press the clutch fully down with the left.
Select first gear and release the parking brake before moving off in the manual-start sequence.
Signal the intended direction, check mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic before moving off.
Ease the clutch to the friction point while looking toward the road rather than at your hands or feet.
Move the right foot from brake to accelerator, add gentle acceleration and finish releasing the clutch slowly.
A forward jerk during a manual start can mean the clutch was released abruptly or too much accelerator was applied.
If the vehicle lurches and stalls during the described manual start, insufficient accelerator input is the stated cause.
Choose gears according to the driving task’s required power and speed; first gear supplies starting power.
The manual gives 15 to 25 miles per hour as a second-gear example, depending on engine power and whether the transmission has 3, 4 or 5 speeds.
Second gear can also be used to start on ice or drive through heavy snow.
For a 3-speed transmission, the manual generally describes third gear for speeds above 25 miles per hour.
For a small-engine vehicle with a 4- or 5-speed transmission, the third-gear example extends to 30 or 40 miles per hour.
The manual describes fourth gear for driving above 35 miles per hour on a flat road.
Uphill driving may require reaching 40 miles per hour or more before selecting fourth or fifth gear.
Before an upshift, accelerate to a speed suitable for the intended gear, press the clutch fully down and release the accelerator.
Complete an upshift by selecting the next higher gear, applying accelerator input and progressively releasing the clutch.
Downshifting can provide more power, assist acceleration or steering, and help slow or stop the vehicle.
Downshifting to slow a descent is advised except when the road is slippery.
For a downshift, release the accelerator and use the brake as well if you want to slow.
